links.outcome: Model performance on ChatGPT-only labels versus radiologist-confirmed reference labels
links.effect: Radiologist reclassified 62 of 297 cases (21%) versus ChatGPT's provisional read; language model AUC fell from ChatGPT-only to radiologist-confirmed labels (BERT-base 0·999 to 0·837), showing self-generated labels inflate performance.
links.quote: The radiologist reclassified 62 of 297 cases (21%) relative to ChatGPT’s provisional read, and a meaningful proportion of raw ChatGPT text was clinically uninterpretable or unsupported by the imaging.

links.outcome: Clinical interpretability and image support of raw ChatGPT-generated findings text
links.effect: A meaningful proportion of raw ChatGPT text was clinically uninterpretable or unsupported by the imaging; 21% of provisional labels were reclassified by the radiologist.
links.quote: The radiologist reclassified 62 of 297 cases (21%) relative to ChatGPT’s provisional read, and a meaningful proportion of raw ChatGPT text was clinically uninterpretable or unsupported by the imaging.

links.outcome: Apparent benchmark performance of raw AI text versus verified performance
links.effect: Raw ChatGPT text gave language-model AUC 0·992 to 1·000, but performance fell substantially against radiologist-confirmed labels (BERT-base AUC 0·999 to 0·837), overstating true competence.
links.quote: On the 297-case pre/post analysis, this advantage depended heavily on label source: language and text-derived VLM performance fell substantially from ChatGPT-only to radiologist-confirmed labels (e.g. BERT-base AUC 0·999 to 0·837), while vision-model performance was stable or modestly improved (e.g. DenseNet-121 0·867 to 0·891).

unlisted_practices: Reporting multimodal AI performance separately by modality and label provenance (raw AI-generated versus radiologist-verified text)

screen.practice: radiologist verification of AI-generated text and labels
screen.reason: The study directly tests and compares performance outcomes with raw unverified AI-generated text/labels versus radiologist-verified text and labels, examining how this verification practice prevents overestimating multimodal AI diagnostic performance.
